verses.1: "O Rambha you must entice Viswamitra by lust and passion. This important work must be done by you in the interest of the gods".
verses.2: O Rama, to these words of the sagacious, thousandeyed Lord of the gods (Indra) that apsara with folded hands bashfully replied:
verses.3: 'Lord of the devatas this mighty ascetic Viswamitra is a terrible person. He will ceratinly release on his dreadful anger (curse me). O Lord this is my apprehension. You should excuse me'.
verses.4: O Rama having heard Rambha trembling in fear and standing with folded palms, Indra spoke:
verses.5: 'O Rambha have no fear. Feel safe. Carry out my order. When the trees look so beautiful in spring I shall in captivating the form of a cuckoo, stay by your side in the company of Kamadeva (Cupid).
verses.6: 'O Rambha have no fear. Feel safe. Carry out my order. When the trees look so beautiful in spring I shall in captivating the form of a cuckoo, stay by your side in the company of Kamadeva (Cupid).
verses.7: O Rambha displaying many (romantic) gestures and assuming a fascinating form, distract the mighty ascetic, Kausika (Viswamitra)'.
verses.8: At these words (of Indra), Rambha, assumed any form of excellent beauty and with a bright smile set out to allure Viswamitra.
verses.9: Excited by the charming warble of the cuckoo, Viswamitra opened his eyes.
verses.10: On hearing the sound of the incomparable song of the cuckoo along with the sight of Rambha, a doubt arose in the mind of the ascetic.
verses.11: Son of Kushika, the eminent ascetic knew it was the work of Indra. Seized with anger, he cursed Rambha:
verses.12: 'O luckless Rambha, since you have endeavoured to distract me from my desire to conquer wrath and passion, you shall turn into a rock and remain so for ten thousand years'.
verses.13: 'O Rambha an effulgent brahmin, endowed with the power of asceticism, will liberate you from this state into which you have fallen on account of my anger'.
verses.14: The brilliant Viswamitra, the great ascetic, now experienced remorse for his inability to contain anger.
verses.15: This mighty curse, of the great saint transformed Rambha into a rock and sent Kamadeva and Indra to their heels.
verses.16: "O Rama highly powerful Viswamitra was deprived of his ascetic merit due to his anger. He had no peace of mind for his inability to control his senses.
verses.17: Having been deprived of his ascetic merit, he resolved not to lose his temper nor ever breathe a word".
verses.18: "Further, I shall not even inhale for hundreds of years. I shall conquer my senses and dry up this body.
verses.19: Until brahminhood is obtained by my austerities, I shall stay without breathing or eating for innumerable years. While performing penance, my limbs shall not undergo deterioration".
verses.20: "O Descendant of Raghu in this way that eminent ascetic took an unprecedented vow to practise penance for a thousand years". इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुष्षष्टितमस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the sixtyfourth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
